title: When you don't make your game with AI but add AI to your game...
author: Opposite_Age_1414
selftext:
I am just like many other guys, I really don't like AI slops and I am sorry to say but on this sub more then 90% are AI sloops nothing else. 

And I don't believe good deep game can be made with AI help, iterating and Vibe Coding. 

I believe Devs needs to know what they are doing, have comprehension of scope, size and architecture of their game. 

But Yeah, I added AI to my game... Didn't even want to post on other subs, because of blind hate towards AI (two letters together) and I knew I would be downvoted to oblivion. 

Whisper turns players voice into text. A local Qwen3 AI answers from game-rule cards. Pocket TTS speaks the answer, and Unreal’s speech solver moves her 3D MetaHuman lips live.

comments.author: fisj
comments.body: I'm going to regret leaving this up, but I will, in the hopes that some nuanced conversation and meeting of minds might come from this. OP, I applaud your use of AI technologies to do something interesting, but please refrain from insulting the community, and understand everyone needs to start somewhere in order to learn and try new things - just like you.

replies.author: Opposite_Age_1414
replies.body:
I am absolutely not insulting community.

I cheer this community and require quality, testing, and getting better!

I have wish listed AI made games that are really good!

Game made with AI or without AI doesn't guarantee that game will be fun or success. Unfortunately 99% of our games are bad, my probably included, and that have nothing to do with AI.

I dislike AI slops, that for sure and posts when people trying to present Opus 5.5 as magical game maker...

  
Edit: Sorry if came as an ass in post, my intention was not to insult community at all!

replies.author: Stinky_You
replies.body: Opus kind of is a magical game maker now that you mention it, it's kind of like a magic wand. It can't really do anything on its own.

comments.author: Ferniclestix
comments.body:
Im going to raise a nuanced counter argument here lol. as the mod requests.

So, I belive that there are uses for AI in both typical human coded projects and those  for which... planning, good structure and  i guess... clean code? might be lacking.

See, me, I'm a 3d artist, animator and game designer. I know how the systems work, I understand the underlying logic of how programming functions but as someone with a learning disability (dyslexia and discalculea) I find it very dificult to learn a programming language, it just doesn't click in my odd brain.

What I can however do is all the game design planning stuff.

So, my projects are basically an AI directed by someone who knows what they are doing and understands alot about gameplay, design, game logic and allll that stuff.

for me, AI is super useful, it lets me try out stuff I simply do not have the money for.  now. code clenlyness wise. oh i know its bad. definately, I fight that thing tooth and nail not to every frame my renders to the ground lol.  but I know those pitfalls and how to avoid them heh.

I think good AI games are just a matter of time, everyone is finding the limits right now. its also unfortunate that in this day and age, slop is the name of the game in many ways, more than just AI right now unfortunately. A return to hand crafted things would be cool, id love my stuff not break every couple of weeks sigh.

anyway, I think there are use cases for AI and even in hand crafted code, certain kinds of AI can be useful. for example programmers often struggle with getting good art assets, some of the stand in art ive seen from programmers ive worked with in the past... my god lol stick figures!, everywhere!   anyway. there are a million ways to skin a cat and AI is the same, its how you use it that counts imo, not hte fact that you used it.

just my thoughts on some of your comments. :)

Also, i love any use of ai chat stuff, love some of those mods for like cyberpunk and skyrim, makes me look forward to future advances. :)

edit: man you should have given her a shodan voice modulator XD  tho how the system shock 1 team did that the first time is cray cray lol

comments.author: FondantIcy866
comments.body: Wait so it's already possible to do this with a local model that a normal computer to run? And it can basically be an LLM instruction manual built in the game you talk to with voice? Even if it was just that and had no game mechanics, that would be very helpful for complex games.

replies.author: Opposite_Age_1414
replies.body: Yes I built her instead of building encyclopedia.

replies.author: FondantIcy866
replies.body: What do you mean by "game-rule cards"? How hard was that to figure out how to make it work? Ideally you'd be able to have an "advisor" that can understand the state of the game too but maybe that's too much data.

replies.author: Opposite_Age_1414
replies.body: All her knowledge come from smal text files I write myself from game bible, short and precise. First when she loads she have around 8000 words in memory, it was optimal performance wise. And that is her basic knowledge. Then if you ask ask something specific, she reach for that specific knowledge card that is up to 150 words, and can lead her to second, than to third, depending what you asked her and what is she talking about or how long answer do you want.
